对SFTSV S片段的分子筛查显示有65个阳性池,对应最低感染率(MIR)为0.06%,其中与牛相关的蜱虫群体显示出最高的MIR(0.09%)。系统发育分析表明,本研究中所有鉴定的菌株均聚类在基因型B2的日本/韩国簇内。七种当代菌株中有六种在核苷酸水平上具有100.00%的同源性,并且与2014年历史国内人类分离株相同,表明在分析的S片段部分区域中存在高度的纵向序列保守性。 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1936358]

papers.title: Complex exposure-response relationships between meteorological factors and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome risk.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease influenced by meteorological factors. This study aimed to characterize the complex exposure-response relationships between multiple meteorological factors and SFTS risk in Anhui Province, China. METHODS: Monthly SFTS cases and meteorological data from 2011 to 2023 were analyzed. Candidate lag structures were evaluated using negative binomial generalized additive models (NB-GAM), followed by Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) to assess the joint and individual effects of meteorological factors. Pairwise interactions were quantified using posterior BKMR interaction contrasts and pooled across cities using random-effects meta-analysis. Regional subgroup analyses were also performed. RESULTS: A total of 5,715 SFTS cases were reported, with 84.74% occurring among farmers, and eight cities accounted for 95.56% of all cases. The lag01 showed the best overall model performance and was selected for BKMR analyses. BKMR revealed heterogeneous joint and individual exposure-response patterns across cities, with average temperature and atmospheric pressure showing prominent contributions. However, formal interaction analyses provided no clear evidence of pairwise interactions, and all ten pooled interaction contrasts had 95% confidence intervals including zero. Regional subgroup analysis suggested a stronger joint meteorological effect in the Jianghuai hilly area [0.27 (95% CI 0.03-0.50)] than in the Southern Mountains Region [0.03 (95% CI -0.08-0.15)]. CONCLUSIONS: Meteorological factors showed complex joint exposure-response relationships with SFTS risk, with substantial geographic variation across Anhui Province. Although no clear pairwise interactions were identified, regional differences in joint meteorological effects highlight the importance of considering local ecological and climatic conditions in SFTS early warning and prevention strategies.

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease influenced by meteorological factors. This study aimed to characterize the complex exposure-response relationships between multiple meteorological factors and SFTS risk in Anhui Province, China. METHODS: Monthly SFTS cases and meteorological data from 2011 to 2023 were analyzed. Candidate lag structures were evaluated using negative binomial generalized additive models (NB-GAM), followed by Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) to assess the joint and individual effects of meteorological factors. Pairwise interactions were quantified using posterior BKMR interaction contrasts and pooled across cities using random-effects meta-analysis. Regional subgroup analyses were also performed. Regional subgroup analysis suggested a stronger joint meteorological effect in the Jianghuai hilly area [0.27 (95% CI 0.03-0.50)] than in the Southern Mountains Region [0.03 (95% CI -0.08-0.15)]. CONCLUSIONS: Meteorological factors showed complex joint exposure-response relationships with SFTS risk, with substantial geographic variation across Anhui Province. Although no clear pairwise interactions were identified, regional differences in joint meteorological effects highlight the importance of considering local ecological and climatic conditions in SFTS early warning and prevention strategies.

The authors concluded that meteorological factors have complex relationships with SFTS risk, showing geographic variation. The findings suggest that local ecological and climatic conditions should be considered in SFTS early warning and prevention strategies. The study's evidence is moderate due to the lack of clear pairwise interaction results and the focus on regional subgroup analyses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 是一种受气象因素影响的新兴人兽共患病。本研究旨在分析安徽省内多种气象因素与发热伴血小板减少综合征风险之间的复杂暴露-反应关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2011年至2023年的每月发热伴血小板减少综合征病例和气象数据进行了分析。共报告了5,715例发热伴血小板减少综合征病例,其中84.74%发生在农民中,八个城市占所有病例的95.56%。
elements_zh.methods: 使用负二项广义可加模型 (NB-GAM) 评估候选滞后结构,随后采用贝叶斯核机器回归 (BKMR) 评估气象因素的联合和个体效应。通过随机效应元分析对城市间的成对交互作用进行量化和汇总。还进行了区域亚组分析。
elements_zh.main_results: lag01表现出最佳的整体模型性能,并被选用于BKMR分析。BKMR揭示了不同城市间存在异质性的联合和个体暴露-反应模式,平均温度和大气压显示出显著的贡献。然而,正式的交互作用分析未提供明确的成对交互证据,且所有十个汇总的交互作用对比的95%置信区间均包含零。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 气象因素与发热伴血小板减少综合征风险之间表现出复杂的联合暴露-反应关系,并且在安徽省内存在显著的地理差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 区域间联合气象效应的差异强调了在发热伴血小板减少综合征早期预警和预防策略中考虑本地生态和气候条件的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据中等,因为本研究侧重于区域亚组分析,并未发现明确的成对交互作用。

papers.title: Genetic characterization of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus in ticks from livestock environments in South Korea
papers.abstract: Introduction Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by the SFTS virus (SFTSV), is a highly fatal tick-borne zoonosis that poses a substantial public health threat. Although livestock husbandry environments represent important ecological settings for viral maintenance and circulation, molecular surveillance within these settings remains insufficient. Methods We conducted an annual systematic entomological and molecular survey from March to October between 2023 and 2025 in South Korea, targeting 204 environments adjacent to cattle, horse, deer, goat, and sheep farms. Results Among 101,006 field-collected ticks, Haemaphysalis longicornis was the most abundant species (90.62%), followed by Haemaphysalis flava (8.20%) and Ixodes nipponensis (1.10%). Molecular screening of the SFTSV S-segment revealed 65 positive pools, corresponding to a minimum infection rate (MIR) of 0.06%, with the highest MIR observed in cattle-associated tick populations (0.09%). Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that all identified strains in this study clustered within the Japanese/Korean clade of genotype B2. Six out of seven contemporary strains shared 100.00% nucleotide identity and were identical to historical domestic human isolates from 2014, demonstrating high longitudinal sequence conservation within the analyzed partial S-segment region. Concurrently, detection of SFTSV strain 24CC401 in I. nipponensis larvae provided indirect field-based evidence consistent with potential transovarial persistence. This larval isolate displayed a distinct molecular profile with a 0.65% nucleotide divergence and two nonsynonymous mutations (G129E and V158E). Discussion Our findings indicate that specific genotype B2 lineages were detected in livestock-adjacent environments, suggesting a potential ecological association with livestock farming. Although the observed sequence conservation may support continued evaluation of conserved S-segment regions for molecular surveillance, the functional significance of the mutations identified in the larval isolate remains to be determined. Continued molecular surveillance may help characterize SFTSV genetic variation in ticks from livestock-associated environments.

analysis.summary_en: This study focuses on the genetic characterization of Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) in ticks from livestock environments in South Korea. The research aimed to understand the ecological association of SFTSV with livestock farming and its genetic variation in these settings. A systematic entomological and molecular survey was conducted from 2023 to 2025, targeting 204 environments adjacent to cattle, horse, deer, goat, and sheep farms. Among 101,006 field-collected ticks, Haemaphysalis longicornis was the most abundant species, followed by Haemaphysalis flava and Ixodes nipponensis. Molecular screening of the SFTSV S-segment revealed 65 positive pools, corresponding to a minimum infection rate (MIR) of 0.06%, with the highest MIR observed in cattle-associated tick populations. However, the functional significance of the mutations in the larval isolate remains unclear. papers.abstract_zh: 引言 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)引起的严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是一种高致死率的蜱媒疾病,对公共卫生构成重大威胁。尽管家畜养殖环境是病毒维持和传播的重要生态场所,但这些环境中病毒的分子特征仍不充分。方法 我们在2023年至2025年3月至10月期间,在韩国进行了年度系统的昆虫学和分子学调查,目标是204个靠近牛、马、鹿、羊和山羊农场的环境。结果 在收集的101,006只蜱虫中,Haemaphysalis longicornis是最丰富的种类(90.62%),其次是Haemaphysalis flava(8.20%)和Ixodes nipponensis(1.10%)。对SFTSV S片段的分子筛查显示有65个阳性池,对应最低感染率(MIR)为0.06%,其中与牛相关的蜱虫群体显示出最高的MIR(0.09%)。系统发育分析表明,本研究中所有鉴定的菌株均聚类在基因型B2的日本/韩国簇内。七种当代菌株中有六种在核苷酸水平上具有100.00%的同源性,并且与2014年历史国内人类分离株相同,表明在分析的S片段部分区域中存在高度的纵向序列保守性。同时,在Ixodes nipponensis幼虫中检测到SFTSV菌株24CC401,提供了与潜在垂直传播一致的间接现场证据。该幼虫分离株表现出独特的分子特征,具有0.65%的核苷酸差异,并且有两个非同义突变(G129E和V158E)。讨论 我们的研究结果表明,在家畜相关环境中检测到了特定的基因型B2菌株,这表明可能存在与家畜养殖的生态关联。尽管观察到的序列保守性可能支持对保守的S片段区域进行持续的分子监测,但该幼虫分离株中发现的非同义突变的功能意义仍需进一步确定。持续的分子监测可能有助于阐明家畜相关环境中蜱虫携带的SFTSV遗传变异。

papers.title: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) likely associated with a bite from a Siberian weasel (Mustela sibirica): a case report from China
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a life-threatening tick-borne viral disease with high mortality and limited treatment options. Understanding its transmission routes is essential for effective prevention and control. Case presentation We report a case of a 55-year-old woman from Dalian, Liaoning Province, China, who developed high fever, malaise and diarrhea five days after being bitten by a Siberian weasel ( Mustela sibirica ). A diagnosis of SFTS was made on day 12 after SFTS virus was detected in peripheral blood by metagenomic next-generation sequencing. Despite timely antiviral and supportive treatment, the patient rapidly progressed to multiple organ dysfunction and had a poor prognosis. She had no known exposure to ticks or other animals, raising strong suspicion of SFTSV transmission through the weasel bite. Conclusion This is a case of SFTS potentially associated with a Mustela sibirica bite, suggesting a possible but unconfirmed zoonotic transmission route. These findings highlight the urgent need for surveillance of animal hosts in endemic regions to better understand transmission pathways.

The findings emphasize the need for animal host surveillance in endemic areas to better understand SFTS transmission. analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A case report was conducted in Dalian, Liaoning Province, China, involving a 55-year-old woman who developed high fever, malaise, and diarrhea five days after being bitten by a Siberian weasel (Mustela sibirica).
analysis_en.methods: SFTS virus was detected in peripheral blood using metagenomic next-generation sequencing on day 12 after the bite. The patient had no known exposure to ticks or other animals.
analysis_en.main_results: The SFTS virus was detected in the patient's peripheral blood on day 12 after the bite. The patient rapidly progressed to multiple organ dysfunction and had a poor prognosis despite timely antiviral and supportive treatment.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The case suggests a possible zoonotic transmission route of SFTS virus through a Siberian weasel bite, although this remains unconfirmed.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the urgent need for surveillance of animal hosts in endemic regions to better understand transmission pathways and improve prevention strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of comparative data and confirmation of the transmission route.

papers.title_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 可能与 Siberian weasel (Mustela sibirica) 咬伤有关:来自中国的病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a life-threatening tick-borne viral disease with high mortality and limited treatment options. Understanding its transmission routes is essential for effective prevention and control. Case presentation We report a case of a 55-year-old woman from Dalian, Liaoning Province, China, who developed high fever, malaise and diarrhea five days after being bitten by a Siberian weasel ( Mustela sibirica ). A diagnosis of SFTS was made on day 12 after SFTS virus was detected in peripheral blood by metagenomic next-generation sequencing. Despite timely antiviral and supportive treatment, the patient rapidly progressed to multiple organ dysfunction and had a poor prognosis. She had no known exposure to ticks or other animals, raising strong suspicion of SFTSV transmission through the weasel bite. Conclusion This is a case of SFTS potentially associated with a Mustela sibirica bite, suggesting a possible but unconfirmed zoonotic transmission route. These findings highlight the urgent need for surveillance of animal hosts in endemic regions to better understand transmission pathways.

papers.title: Preclinical immunogenicity and efficacy of novel mRNA vaccine against severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus
papers.abstract: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne disease caused by Bandavirus dabieense , also known as the SFTS virus (SFTSV). SFTS’ fatality rate is 10%–27%, and SFTS cases and the distribution of outbreaks are increasing, but there is no approved vaccine to prevent SFTS. Here, we examined the immunogenicity and efficacy of three lipid nanoparticle-mRNA (LNP-mRNA) vaccine candidates encoding SFTSV glycoprotein N (Gn), glycoprotein C (Gc), or nucleocapsid protein (NP) (LNP-mRNA-Gn, LNP-mRNA-Gc, and LNP-mRNA-NP, respectively) in mice. Immunization with LNP-mRNA-Gn, LNP-mRNA-Gc, or LNP-mRNA-NP alone completely protected Ifnar1 – / – mice from lethal SFTSV challenge. LNP-mRNA-Gn and LNP-mRNA-Gc also induced SFTSV-neutralizing activity in Ifnar1 – / – mice, whereas LNP-mRNA NP did not. The efficacy of LNP-mRNA-NP was abrogated by the in vivo depletion of CD4 + cells, but not CD8 + cells. These results highlight three promising candidates for effective vaccines against SFTS, each possessing a distinct protective mechanism.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne disease caused by Bandavirus dabieense, also known as the SFTS virus (SFTSV). The study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and efficacy of novel mRNA vaccine candidates against SFTSV.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a preclinical investigation examining three lipid nanoparticle-mRNA (LNP-mRNA) vaccine candidates encoding SFTSV glycoprotein N (Gn), glycoprotein C (Gc), or nucleocapsid protein (NP) in mice. The study was conducted in a laboratory setting using Ifnar1 – / – mice as the host.
analysis.methods: The researchers assessed the immunogenicity and efficacy of the LNP-mRNA vaccine candidates by immunizing mice and then challenging them with lethal SFTSV doses. They evaluated the protective effects and measured SFTSV-neutralizing activity in the mice.
analysis.main_results: Immunization with LNP-mRNA-Gn, LNP-mRNA-Gc, or LNP-mRNA-NP alone completely protected Ifnar1 – / – mice from lethal SFTSV challenge. LNP-mRNA-Gn and LNP-mRNA-Gc also induced SFTSV-neutralizing activity in Ifnar1 – / – mice, whereas LNP-mRNA-NP did not.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results indicate that all three vaccine candidates are promising for developing effective vaccines against SFTSV, with each possessing a distinct protective mechanism.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide important insights into the development of vaccines for SFTSV, which could contribute to surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for SFTS.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to preclinical models and does not include human trials. The evidence is strong based on the complete protection observed in mice, but further research is needed to confirm efficacy in humans.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the immunogenicity and efficacy of three novel mRNA vaccine candidates against Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), a tick-borne pathogen causing SFTS. The researchers tested the vaccines in mice and found that all three candidates provided complete protection against lethal SFTSV challenge. LNP-mRNA-Gn and LNP-mRNA-Gc also induced neutralizing activity, while LNP-mRNA-NP did not. The efficacy of LNP-mRNA-NP was dependent on CD4+ cells, highlighting distinct protective mechanisms among the candidates. These results suggest potential vaccine development strategies for SFTSV, though further human studies are necessary. The study is limited to preclinical models, which may affect the generalizability of findings.

news.content: Back to Journals » Infection and Drug Resistance » Volume 19 Authors Liu S , Kong H , Wang Y , Pan J , Niu H , Zhao D Accepted for publication 2 September 2026 Published 19 September 2026 Volume 2026:19 633745 DOI https://doi.org/10.2147/IDR.S633745 Review by Single anonymous peer review Editor who approved publication: Dr Sandip Patil Shuting Liu, 1, * Haobo Kong, 2, * Yun Wang, 1 Jingjing Pan, 2 Hua Niu, 1 Dahai Zhao 1 1 Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Anhui Chest Hospital, Hefei, Anhui, People’s Republic of China; 2 Department of Respiratory Intensive Care Unit, Anhui Chest Hospital, Hefei, Anhui, People’s Republic of China *These authors contributed equally to this work Correspondence: Hua Niu; Dahai Zhao, Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Anhui Chest Hospital, No. 397 Jixi Road, Hefei, Anhui, 23000, People’s Republic of China, Email niuhua2025@163.com; zhaodahai@ahmu.edu.cn Background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne viral disease characterized by severe immune dysregulation and high mortality, predisposing patients to opportunistic infections. Case Presentation: We report a 76-year-old male patient diagnosed with SFTS complicated by chronic hepatitis B with low-level viral replication, liver injury, and myocardial injury. After initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, hepatoprotective therapy, and antiviral therapy, the patient stabilized. During hospitalization, he developed pulmonary infection. Sputum culture was positive for Aspergillus fumigatus and serum galactomannan (GM) test was positive. Initial treatment with voriconazole led to radiological improvement in the right lung lesion; however, progression of the left lung lesion was observed. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified Rhizopus microsporus, leading to the diagnosis of invasive pulmonary Aspergillus–Mucorales coinfection. Oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B was administered, resulting in significant clinical and radiological improvement. Approximately one month after isavuconazole therapy, the patient developed jaundice and coagulation dysfunction. After exclusion of hepatitis B virus reactivation and other potential causes, isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury was considered probable based on the clinical course and a RUCAM score of 8. Conclusion: SFTS patients are highly susceptible to invasive fungal infections due to immune dysregulation, thrombocytopenia, and endothelial injury. Clinicians should consider mucormycosis in patients with poor response to voriconazole and progressive pulmonary lesions, and early bronchoscopy with mNGS is recommended. Although isavuconazole is considered relatively safe, liver function monitoring is essential, especially in patients with underlying liver disease. Keywords: severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, mucormycosis, mixed fungal infection, isavuconazole, drug-induced liver injury Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an acute tick-borne infectious disease caused by infection with the severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV). It is primarily transmitted through tick bites and is clinically characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and multiple organ dysfunction. The case fatality rate ranges from 10% to 30%. 1 SFTS is mainly endemic in East Asian countries, including China, Japan, and South Korea, with the highest number of reported cases in China, predominantly in rural mountainous and hilly regions. 2 Recent studies have shown that, in addition to direct viral injury, SFTSV infection can induce profound immune dysregulation, including lymphocyte depletion, impaired cellular immunity, macrophage dysfunction, and excessive inflammatory responses. These immune abnormalities may increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections, particularly invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA). 3 However, reports of SFTS complicated by mixed Aspergillus and Mucorales infections are extremely rare, and both diagnosis and treatment remain highly challenging. Isavuconazole is a newer-generation broad-spectrum triazole antifungal agent with potent activity against Aspergillus species and Mucorales. It has been approved for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis and has become an important therapeutic option for patients with invasive mold infections, especially those who are intolerant of or have an inadequate response to conventional antifungal therapies. 4 , 5 Compared with voriconazole, isavuconazole exhibits more predictable pharmacokinetic characteristics, fewer drug–drug interactions, and improved tolerability, with a lower frequency of hepatobiliary adverse events. 4 Therefore, isavuconazole is increasingly used in patients requiring prolonged antifungal treatment or with complex clinical conditions. However, despite its favorable safety profile, clinically significant isavuconazole-associated liver injury, including cholestatic and mixed-pattern injury, has been reported. 6 In patients with hepatitis B virus infection, SFTS-related systemic inflammatory response, and polypharmacy, hepatic injury may still be induced or exacerbated. Here, we report a case of SFTS complicated by invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and mucormycosis coinfection, together with isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury, to enhance clinicians’ awareness of such complex clinical scenarios. A 76-year-old male presented with a 5-day history of fever, fatigue, and anorexia on May 27, 2025. The patient had been engaged in agricultural work prior to disease onset and had no significant past medical history. Initial laboratory investigations revealed a platelet count of 19 × 10 9 /L and a white blood cell count of 3.2 × 10 9 /L. Liver function tests showed elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels of 433 U/L and 837 U/L, respectively, while the creatine kinase (CK) level was 3437 U/L. The serum albumin level was 28.6 g/L. SFTSV RNA was positive. Serological testing showed positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and negative HIV antibody, and the HBV DNA level was 60.5 IU/mL. The patient was diagnosed with SFTS, chronic hepatitis B with low-level viral replication, liver injury, and myocardial injury. Subsequently, the patient developed persistent high fever and worsening thrombocytopenia, with the platelet count decreasing to 12 × 10 9 /L. Liver enzymes and coagulation parameters progressively worsened. After immunoglobulin (25 g/day for 5 days), entecavir, and supportive therapy, the patient’s clinical condition stabilized, and the liver function and complete blood count gradually returned to near-normal levels. Recombinant granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (rhG-CSF) was not administered during hospitalization. During hospitalization, cough and sputum production developed. Sputum culture identified Aspergillus fumigatus, and GM test was positive. Chest CT showed bilateral pulmonary lesions ( Figure 1A and B ). Voriconazole antifungal therapy was administered for over two months. Follow-up chest CT showed absorption of right lung lesions but progressive consolidation in left lung lesions. Broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy with meropenem, ceftriaxone, and levofloxacin failed to reverse left lung lesion progression ( Figure 1C and D ). Breakthrough mucormycosis was suspected during voriconazole therapy due to progressive lesions. Bronchoscopy revealed a necrotic, friable endobronchial mass ( Figure 2A and B ). mNGS detected Rhizopus microsporus (a Mucorales fungus), Acinetobacter baumannii, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Staphylococcus haemolyticus. A diagnosis of invasive pulmonary Aspergillus–Mucorales coinfection was established. Treatment with oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B was initiated, resulting in significant clinical improvement and radiological regression after 2 weeks. Nebulized amphotericin B was subsequently discontinued, and isavuconazole was continued as the sole antifungal agent. Figure 1 Chest computed tomography (CT) images of the patient. ( A and B ) Chest CT taken on June 24, 2025: Multiple nodular and patchy shadows in both lungs, bilateral pleural thickening, and bilateral pleural effusion. ( C and D ) Chest CT taken on September 29, 2025: The lesion in the right lung has shown absorption, while the lesion in the left upper lung has significantly progressed with an increased area of consolidation; there is a small amount of pleural effusion on the left side. ( E and F ) Chest CT taken on January 7, 2026: The left lung lesion shows significant absorption, and the left pleural effusion has further decreased. Figure 2 Bronchoscopy images of the patient. ( A and B ) Bronchoscopy performed on September 25, 2025: A long cord-like lesion was observed in the upper lobe bronchus of the left lung, covered with gray-black sputum, and prone to bleeding upon palpation. After approximately 1 month of isavuconazole therapy, the patient developed jaundice and coagulation abnormalities. Laboratory tests showed an ALT level of 902 U/L, an AST level of 712 U/L, and a total bilirubin level of 217 μmol/L, accompanied by prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and an elevated international normalized ratio (INR). The HBV DNA level remained low at 35.2 IU/mL, with no evidence of hepatitis B virus reactivation. After exclusion of hepatitis B virus reactivation and other potential causes, isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury was considered the most likely cause of the marked hepatic deterioration. Isavuconazole was discontinued, and the patient received comprehensive hepatoprotective treatment, including artificial liver support therapy, glutathione, ursodeoxycholic acid, and other supportive measures. Liver function gradually recovered after these interventions. Due to lack of alternatives, isavuconazole was cautiously reintroduced under strict monitoring without recurrence of severe hepatotoxicity, and pulmonary lesions ultimately resolved after two months ( Figure 1E and F ). The clinical course, treatment timeline, and outcomes are summarized in Table 1 . Table 1 Clinical Timeline, Treatment Course, and Outcomes of the Patient Recent studies have demonstrated that, in addition to direct viral damage, immune dysfunction induced by SFTSV is a major contributor to secondary opportunistic infections in patients with SFTS. 7 SFTS is primarily characterized by cell-mediated immune impairment. SFTSV infection may lead to T-cell exhaustion and lymphopenia, cytokine imbalance, and dysfunction of macrophages and dendritic cells, all of which markedly impair host antifungal immunity. 8 It has been reported that CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts are significantly reduced in patients with severe SFTS, and these reductions are closely associated with disease severity and mortality risk. 9 Platelets not only participate in the hemostatic process but also play a critical role in anti-infective immunity. A decrease in platelet count further impairs the bactericidal capacity of neutrophils and macrophages, while disruption of the endothelial barrier increases the risk of pathogen invasion. 10 , 11 The risk of secondary fungal or bacterial infections increases significantly in SFTS patients with platelet counts <50 × 10 9 /L. 12 These immune alterations likely contributed to the development of invasive fungal coinfection in the present case. IVIG was administered during the acute phase of SFTS (25 g/day for 5 days) as an immunomodulatory therapy. However, invasive pulmonary Aspergillus and Mucorales infections subsequently developed, suggesting that SFTSV-associated immune dysfunction may persist despite supportive immunotherapy. In addition, hypoalbuminemia (albumin 28.6 g/L) was observed during the acute phase. Reduced serum albumin levels may potentially influence the pharmacokinetic characteristics of highly protein-bound drugs; however, therapeutic drug monitoring of isavuconazole was unavailable in this case. Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is one of the most common secondary fungal infections in SFTS. Studies indicate that the incidence of IPA in SFTS patients is approximately 30%, with significantly increased mortality rates observed in patients co-infected with Aspergillus species. 13 In this case, right lung lesions improved after voriconazole treatment, whereas left lung lesions continued to progress and showed poor response to broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy. Ultimately, Rhizopus microsporus was identified in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid using metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), consistent with breakthrough mucormycosis. Recent studies suggest that prolonged exposure to broad-spectrum antibiotics may disrupt intestinal and respiratory microbiota homeostasis through the gut–lung axis. 14 , 15 This may have contributed to the development of breakthrough mucormycosis in this patient. In addition, persistent immunosuppression following SFTSV infection may further promote invasive growth of Mucorales. Although breakthrough mucormycosis has been widely reported in COVID-19-associated fungal infections, it remains relatively rare in SFTS. 16 In this case, early sputum culture only detected Aspergillus fumigatus, while subsequent NGS analysis of lavage fluid identified Rhizopus microsporus, highlighting the limited sensitivity of conventional sputum culture for deep pulmonary Aspergillus infections. For SFTS patients, particularly those with severe thrombocytopenia, progressive pulmonary lesions, or poor response to voriconazole therapy, breakthrough mycotic infections should be suspected; mNGS aids in early etiological diagnosis. This patient had a pre-existing chronic hepatitis B background and had experienced SFTSV infection, multiple infections, and prolonged anti-infective therapy, leading to a progressive decline in hepatic reserve function. After approximately one month of isavuconazole treatment, the patient developed significant jaundice, elevated transaminase levels, coagulation disorders, with total bilirubin rising to 217.0 μmol/L and PT and APTT markedly prolonged, indicating severe liver injury accompanied by pronounced coagulation abnormalities and a trend toward progression to liver failure. The patient’s HBV-DNA levels remained consistently low, with no evidence of viral reactivation or other definitive factors of liver injury such as biliary obstruction. In addition, nebulized amphotericin B had been discontinued, and isavuconazole was the only ongoing antifungal agent at the time of hepatic deterioration. Following discontinuation of isavuconazole and initiation of supportive therapies including artificial liver support, liver function and coagulation parameters gradually improved. Notably, the patient’s liver function gradually recovered after discontinuation of isavuconazole and initiation of artificial liver support therapy. Given the need for continued antifungal treatment and the limited therapeutic alternatives, isavuconazole was subsequently reintroduced under close monitoring of liver function and coagulation parameters. news.content_original: Back to Journals » Infection and Drug Resistance » Volume 19 Authors Liu S , Kong H , Wang Y , Pan J , Niu H , Zhao D Accepted for publication 2 September 2026 Published 19 September 2026 Volume 2026:19 633745 DOI https://doi.org/10.2147/IDR.S633745 Review by Single anonymous peer review Editor who approved publication: Dr Sandip Patil Shuting Liu, 1, * Haobo Kong, 2, * Yun Wang, 1 Jingjing Pan, 2 Hua Niu, 1 Dahai Zhao 1 1 Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Anhui Chest Hospital, Hefei, Anhui, People’s Republic of China; 2 Department of Respiratory Intensive Care Unit, Anhui Chest Hospital, Hefei, Anhui, People’s Republic of China *These authors contributed equally to this work Correspondence: Hua Niu; Dahai Zhao, Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Anhui Chest Hospital, No. 397 Jixi Road, Hefei, Anhui, 23000, People’s Republic of China, Email niuhua2025@163.com; zhaodahai@ahmu.edu.cn Background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne viral disease characterized by severe immune dysregulation and high mortality, predisposing patients to opportunistic infections. Case Presentation: We report a 76-year-old male patient diagnosed with SFTS complicated by chronic hepatitis B with low-level viral replication, liver injury, and myocardial injury. After initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, hepatoprotective therapy, and antiviral therapy, the patient stabilized. During hospitalization, he developed pulmonary infection. Sputum culture was positive for Aspergillus fumigatus and serum galactomannan (GM) test was positive. Initial treatment with voriconazole led to radiological improvement in the right lung lesion; however, progression of the left lung lesion was observed. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified Rhizopus microsporus, leading to the diagnosis of invasive pulmonary Aspergillus–Mucorales coinfection. Oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B was administered, resulting in significant clinical and radiological improvement. Approximately one month after isavuconazole therapy, the patient developed jaundice and coagulation dysfunction. After exclusion of hepatitis B virus reactivation and other potential causes, isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury was considered probable based on the clinical course and a RUCAM score of 8. Conclusion: SFTS patients are highly susceptible to invasive fungal infections due to immune dysregulation, thrombocytopenia, and endothelial injury. Clinicians should consider mucormycosis in patients with poor response to voriconazole and progressive pulmonary lesions, and early bronchoscopy with mNGS is recommended. Although isavuconazole is considered relatively safe, liver function monitoring is essential, especially in patients with underlying liver disease. Keywords: severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, mucormycosis, mixed fungal infection, isavuconazole, drug-induced liver injury Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an acute tick-borne infectious disease caused by infection with the severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV). It is primarily transmitted through tick bites and is clinically characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and multiple organ dysfunction. The case fatality rate ranges from 10% to 30%. 1 SFTS is mainly endemic in East Asian countries, including China, Japan, and South Korea, with the highest number of reported cases in China, predominantly in rural mountainous and hilly regions. 2 Recent studies have shown that, in addition to direct viral injury, SFTSV infection can induce profound immune dysregulation, including lymphocyte depletion, impaired cellular immunity, macrophage dysfunction, and excessive inflammatory responses. These immune abnormalities may increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections, particularly invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA). 3 However, reports of SFTS complicated by mixed Aspergillus and Mucorales infections are extremely rare, and both diagnosis and treatment remain highly challenging. Isavuconazole is a newer-generation broad-spectrum triazole antifungal agent with potent activity against Aspergillus species and Mucorales. It has been approved for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis and has become an important therapeutic option for patients with invasive mold infections, especially those who are intolerant of or have an inadequate response to conventional antifungal therapies. 4 , 5 Compared with voriconazole, isavuconazole exhibits more predictable pharmacokinetic characteristics, fewer drug–drug interactions, and improved tolerability, with a lower frequency of hepatobiliary adverse events. 4 Therefore, isavuconazole is increasingly used in patients requiring prolonged antifungal treatment or with complex clinical conditions. However, despite its favorable safety profile, clinically significant isavuconazole-associated liver injury, including cholestatic and mixed-pattern injury, has been reported. 6 In patients with hepatitis B virus infection, SFTS-related systemic inflammatory response, and polypharmacy, hepatic injury may still be induced or exacerbated. Here, we report a case of SFTS complicated by invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and mucormycosis coinfection, together with isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury, to enhance clinicians’ awareness of such complex clinical scenarios. A 76-year-old male presented with a 5-day history of fever, fatigue, and anorexia on May 27, 2025. The patient had been engaged in agricultural work prior to disease onset and had no significant past medical history. Initial laboratory investigations revealed a platelet count of 19 × 10 9 /L and a white blood cell count of 3.2 × 10 9 /L. Liver function tests showed elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels of 433 U/L and 837 U/L, respectively, while the creatine kinase (CK) level was 3437 U/L. The serum albumin level was 28.6 g/L. SFTSV RNA was positive. Serological testing showed positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and negative HIV antibody, and the HBV DNA level was 60.5 IU/mL. The patient was diagnosed with SFTS, chronic hepatitis B with low-level viral replication, liver injury, and myocardial injury. Subsequently, the patient developed persistent high fever and worsening thrombocytopenia, with the platelet count decreasing to 12 × 10 9 /L. Liver enzymes and coagulation parameters progressively worsened. After immunoglobulin (25 g/day for 5 days), entecavir, and supportive therapy, the patient’s clinical condition stabilized, and the liver function and complete blood count gradually returned to near-normal levels. Recombinant granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (rhG-CSF) was not administered during hospitalization. During hospitalization, cough and sputum production developed. Sputum culture identified Aspergillus fumigatus, and GM test was positive. Chest CT showed bilateral pulmonary lesions ( Figure 1A and B ). Voriconazole antifungal therapy was administered for over two months. Follow-up chest CT showed absorption of right lung lesions but progressive consolidation in left lung lesions. Broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy with meropenem, ceftriaxone, and levofloxacin failed to reverse left lung lesion progression ( Figure 1C and D ). Breakthrough mucormycosis was suspected during voriconazole therapy due to progressive lesions. Bronchoscopy revealed a necrotic, friable endobronchial mass ( Figure 2A and B ). mNGS detected Rhizopus microsporus (a Mucorales fungus), Acinetobacter baumannii, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Staphylococcus haemolyticus. A diagnosis of invasive pulmonary Aspergillus–Mucorales coinfection was established. Treatment with oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B was initiated, resulting in significant clinical improvement and radiological regression after 2 weeks. Nebulized amphotericin B was subsequently discontinued, and isavuconazole was continued as the sole antifungal agent. Figure 1 Chest computed tomography (CT) images of the patient. ( A and B ) Chest CT taken on June 24, 2025: Multiple nodular and patchy shadows in both lungs, bilateral pleural thickening, and bilateral pleural effusion. ( C and D ) Chest CT taken on September 29, 2025: The lesion in the right lung has shown absorption, while the lesion in the left upper lung has significantly progressed with an increased area of consolidation; there is a small amount of pleural effusion on the left side. ( E and F ) Chest CT taken on January 7, 2026: The left lung lesion shows significant absorption, and the left pleural effusion has further decreased. Figure 2 Bronchoscopy images of the patient. ( A and B ) Bronchoscopy performed on September 25, 2025: A long cord-like lesion was observed in the upper lobe bronchus of the left lung, covered with gray-black sputum, and prone to bleeding upon palpation. After approximately 1 month of isavuconazole therapy, the patient developed jaundice and coagulation abnormalities. Laboratory tests showed an ALT level of 902 U/L, an AST level of 712 U/L, and a total bilirubin level of 217 μmol/L, accompanied by prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and an elevated international normalized ratio (INR). The HBV DNA level remained low at 35.2 IU/mL, with no evidence of hepatitis B virus reactivation. After exclusion of hepatitis B virus reactivation and other potential causes, isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury was considered the most likely cause of the marked hepatic deterioration. Isavuconazole was discontinued, and the patient received comprehensive hepatoprotective treatment, including artificial liver support therapy, glutathione, ursodeoxycholic acid, and other supportive measures. Liver function gradually recovered after these interventions. Due to lack of alternatives, isavuconazole was cautiously reintroduced under strict monitoring without recurrence of severe hepatotoxicity, and pulmonary lesions ultimately resolved after two months ( Figure 1E and F ). The clinical course, treatment timeline, and outcomes are summarized in Table 1 . Table 1 Clinical Timeline, Treatment Course, and Outcomes of the Patient Recent studies have demonstrated that, in addition to direct viral damage, immune dysfunction induced by SFTSV is a major contributor to secondary opportunistic infections in patients with SFTS. 7 SFTS is primarily characterized by cell-mediated immune impairment. SFTSV infection may lead to T-cell exhaustion and lymphopenia, cytokine imbalance, and dysfunction of macrophages and dendritic cells, all of which markedly impair host antifungal immunity. 8 It has been reported that CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts are significantly reduced in patients with severe SFTS, and these reductions are closely associated with disease severity and mortality risk. 9 Platelets not only participate in the hemostatic process but also play a critical role in anti-infective immunity. A decrease in platelet count further impairs the bactericidal capacity of neutrophils and macrophages, while disruption of the endothelial barrier increases the risk of pathogen invasion. 10 , 11 The risk of secondary fungal or bacterial infections increases significantly in SFTS patients with platelet counts <50 × 10 9 /L. 12 These immune alterations likely contributed to the development of invasive fungal coinfection in the present case. IVIG was administered during the acute phase of SFTS (25 g/day for 5 days) as an immunomodulatory therapy. However, invasive pulmonary Aspergillus and Mucorales infections subsequently developed, suggesting that SFTSV-associated immune dysfunction may persist despite supportive immunotherapy. In addition, hypoalbuminemia (albumin 28.6 g/L) was observed during the acute phase. Reduced serum albumin levels may potentially influence the pharmacokinetic characteristics of highly protein-bound drugs; however, therapeutic drug monitoring of isavuconazole was unavailable in this case. Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is one of the most common secondary fungal infections in SFTS. Studies indicate that the incidence of IPA in SFTS patients is approximately 30%, with significantly increased mortality rates observed in patients co-infected with Aspergillus species. 13 In this case, right lung lesions improved after voriconazole treatment, whereas left lung lesions continued to progress and showed poor response to broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy. Ultimately, Rhizopus microsporus was identified in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid using metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), consistent with breakthrough mucormycosis. In addition, persistent immunosuppression following SFTSV infection may further promote invasive growth of Mucorales. Although breakthrough mucormycosis has been widely reported in COVID-19-associated fungal infections, it remains relatively rare in SFTS. 16 In this case, early sputum culture only detected Aspergillus fumigatus, while subsequent NGS analysis of lavage fluid identified Rhizopus microsporus, highlighting the limited sensitivity of conventional sputum culture for deep pulmonary Aspergillus infections. For SFTS patients, particularly those with severe thrombocytopenia, progressive pulmonary lesions, or poor response to voriconazole therapy, breakthrough mycotic infections should be suspected; mNGS aids in early etiological diagnosis. This patient had a pre-existing chronic hepatitis B background and had experienced SFTSV infection, multiple infections, and prolonged anti-infective therapy, leading to a progressive decline in hepatic reserve function. Given the need for continued antifungal treatment and the limited therapeutic alternatives, isavuconazole was subsequently reintroduced under close monitoring of liver function and coagulation parameters. analysis_en.time: The article was published on 19 September 2026. The event date is May 27, 2025, when the patient presented with symptoms.
analysis_en.location_and_population: The case was reported in Hefei, Anhui, People’s Republic of China. The patient was a 76-year-old male with a history of agricultural work and chronic hepatitis B.
analysis_en.event: A 76-year-old male patient was diagnosed with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) complicated by invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and mucormycosis coinfection, along with isavuconazole-associated drug-induced liver injury.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: The case highlights the risk of invasive fungal infections in SFTS patients due to immune dysregulation. The patient experienced liver injury, which was considered probable based on clinical course and RUCAM score of 8. The case fatality rate for SFTS ranges from 10% to 30%.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The patient received treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, hepatoprotective therapy, antiviral therapy, and later oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B. The treatment led to significant clinical and radiological improvement. Liver function monitoring was emphasized, especially in patients with underlying liver disease.

news.title_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征合并侵袭性肺曲霉菌病 | IDR - dovepress.com
news.source_body_en: This article reports a case of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in a 76-year-old male patient from Hefei, Anhui, China, who presented with fever, fatigue, and anorexia on May 27, 2025. The patient had a history of agricultural work and chronic hepatitis B with low-level viral replication. He was diagnosed with SFTS, liver injury, myocardial injury, and invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and mucormycosis coinfection. Initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, hepatoprotective therapy, and antiviral therapy stabilized his condition. Subsequently, he was treated with oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B, which led to significant clinical and radiological improvement. However, approximately one month after isavuconazole therapy, the patient developed jaundice and coagulation dysfunction, which were considered probable as drug-induced liver injury. The case underscores the susceptibility of SFTS patients to invasive fungal infections due to immune dysregulation and highlights the importance of liver function monitoring in such patients. The case fatality rate for SFTS ranges from 10% to 30%, and the patient's condition improved with the treatment, with pulmonary lesions resolving after two months.
news.content_zh: 本文报道了一例来自中国安徽省合肥市的76岁男性患者,于2025年5月27日出现发热、乏力和食欲减退症状,诊断为发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征),并伴有侵袭性肺曲霉菌病和毛霉菌病的合并感染。初始使用治疗联合静脉注射免疫球蛋白、保肝治疗和抗病毒药物治疗稳定了病情。随后,患者接受了口服异瓦康唑联合雾化两性霉素B治疗,临床和影像学症状显著改善。然而,在异瓦康唑治疗约一个月后,患者出现黄疸和凝血功能障碍,考虑为药物性肝损伤的可能性较高。该病例强调了发热伴血小板减少综合征患者由于免疫失调而容易发生侵袭性真菌感染的风险,并突出了对这类患者进行肝功能监测的重要性。发热伴血小板减少综合征的病死率范围为10%至30%,患者在使用治疗后病情改善,肺部病变在两个月后消退。

syndrome,SFTS)是一种受气象因素影响的新发蜱传传染病。本研究旨在刻画中国安徽省多种气象因素与SFTS风险之间的复杂暴露-反应关系。 方法:研究人员分 目的:发热伴血小板减少综合征(severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome,SFTS)是一种受气象因素影响的新发蜱传传染病。本研究旨在刻画中国安徽省多种气象因素与SFTS风险之间的复杂暴露-反应关系。 方法:研究人员分析了2011年至2023年的月度SFTS病例及气象数据。采用负二项广义加性模型(negative binomial generalized additive model,NB-GAM)评估候选滞后结构,随后应用贝叶斯核机器回归(Bayesian kernel machine regression,BKMR)评估气象因素的联合效应与单独效应。基于后验BKMR交互对比量化两两交互作用,并通过随机效应meta分析在各城市间进行合并。此外,还进行了区域亚组分析。 结果:共报告5,715例SFTS病例,其中84.74%为农民,8个城市占全部病例的95.56%。lag01在所有候选滞后结构中表现出最佳整体模型性能,并被选用于BKMR分析。BKMR揭示了各城市间异质性的联合及单独暴露-反应模式,其中平均气温和大气压贡献突出。然而,正式的交互作用分析未提供清晰的两两交互证据,全部10个合并交互对比的95%置信区间均包含零。区域亚组分析提示,江淮丘陵区的联合气象效应[0.27(95% CI 0.03–0.50)]强于皖南山区[0.03(95% CI ?0.08–0.15)]。 结论:气象因素与SFTS风险之间存在复杂的联合暴露-反应关系,且安徽省内存在显著的地理变异。尽管未识别出清晰的两两交互作用,但联合气象效应的区域差异凸显了在SFTS预警和防控策略中考虑当地生态与气候条件的重要性。 一、研究背景与问题提出 发热伴血小板减少综合征(severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome,SFTS)是由大别班达病毒(Dabie bandavirus,DBV)引起的新发蜱传人畜共患病,已成为东亚地区特别是中国重要的公共卫生威胁。该病以高热、血小板减少、白细胞减少和多器官功能障碍为主要特征,病死率高达16.2%。自2009年首次发现以来,SFTS已在中国超过25个省份报告,安徽省是高度流行区之一。长角血蜱(Haemaphysalis longicornis)作为DBV的主要传播媒介,其生存、繁殖能力和宿主搜寻行为深受气象条件影响。 既往研究多聚焦于单一气象因素与SFTS发病的关联,忽视了多气象因素共同作用的联合效应及其潜在交互影响。气象变量并非孤立作用,而是构成相互关联的系统,某一因素的变化可能增强或削弱其他因素的影响。此外,植被覆盖、土地利用和社会经济状况等非气象因素也可能改变气候与SFTS风险之间的关系,但这些协变量很少被纳入综合风险评估模型。同时,气象因素对SFTS发病的影响可能存在显著的时间滞后效应,选择合适的暴露滞后窗口是评估气象因素混合效应的关键前提。基于此,本研究利用安徽省2011—2023年8个SFTS高发城市的月度面板数据,系统评估多种气象因素与SFTS风险的复杂暴露-反应关系。 二、研究设计与方法概述 研究人员从中国疾病预防控制中心国家传染病报告信息管理系统获取2011—2023年安徽省月度SFTS病例数据,从中国气象数据服务中心提取5项气象变量的逐日数据并转换为月均值,同时收集了人均GDP、归一化植被指数(Normalized Difference Vegetation Index,NDVI)、城市化率和土地利用类型等协变量数据。研究首先采用负二项广义加性模型(negative binomial generalized additive model,NB-GAM)对6种预设滞后结构进行筛选,基于赤池信息准则(Akaike Information Criterion,AIC)和偏差解释度确定最优滞后窗口;随后构建贝叶斯核机器回归(Bayesian kernel machine regression,BKMR)模型,通过高斯核函数非参数估计暴露-反应函数,采用slab-and-spike先验进行变量选择,以后验包含概率(Posterior Inclusion Probability,PIP)量化各气象变量的相对重要性,并通过后验交互对比评估两两交互作用。各城市结果通过随机效应meta分析进行合并,并依据安徽省自然地理分区开展区域亚组分析。 三、研究结果 流行病学特征:2011—2023年安徽省共报告5,715例SFTS病例,居全国第三位,其中84.74%为农民。累计病例数超过100例的8个城市(滁州、六安、合肥、安庆、马鞍山、宣城、铜陵、池州)占全省报告病例的95.56%。病例时间分布主要集中在4至7月。 滞后结构选择:城市特异性NB-GAM结果显示,lag01在8个城市中的5个取得最低AIC值,且平均偏差解释度最高(69.9%)。基于模型诊断结果和跨城市一致性,lag01被选定为后续BKMR建模的标准暴露窗口。 变量重要性:PIP结果显示,大气压(平均PIP=0.747)和平均气温(平均PIP=0.735)在所有8个城市中均超过0.5阈值,表现出最高的跨城市平均重要性;降水重要性中等,相对湿度和风速重要性较低。 单独效应:平均气温在多数城市呈倒U型暴露-反应模式,在中位暴露水平的meta分析中显示最大的正向效应(0.034,95% CI 0.010–0.057,P=0.005);大气压亦呈现显著正向效应(0.025,95% CI 0.007–0.042,P=0.006);相对湿度、风速和降水的关联较弱且未达统计学显著。 联合效应与交互作用:8个城市中6个(75%)显示正向联合效应,整体联合效应为0.078(95% CI ?0.032–0.187,P=0.164),呈正向但未达显著。10个两两交互对比的合并估计均包含零,未发现清晰的两两交互证据,城市间异质性低。 区域亚组分析:江淮丘陵区的联合气象效应为0.27(95% CI 0.03–0.50),呈统计学显著正向关联;皖南山区为0.03(95% CI ?0.08–0.15),未达显著。meta回归显示区域间差异未达统计学显著(β=?0.234,95% CI ?0.505–0.037,P=0.087)。 四、讨论与结论 研究发现气象因素对SFTS风险的影响表现为短期滞后效应、非线性暴露-反应关系及显著的地理变异。lag01暴露窗口的生物学合理性在于气象条件可短期内影响长角血蜱的活动、存活和宿主搜寻行为,实验室研究已证实长角血蜱的存活温度阈值为12–40°C,野外观察显示其日活动高峰出现在25–40°C并最活跃于35°C。平均气温和大气压是最重要的气象因素,气温的倒U型关系与蜱传传播的生态特征相符,适宜温度促进蜱的发育和宿主搜寻行为,而过高的温度可能通过增加水分流失抑制蜱的活动。大气压的高显著性可能反映整体天气背景而非对蜱或病原体的直接效应。相对湿度、风速和降水效应较弱但并非生态学上不重要,其效应可能依赖当地气候、地形和植被条件。条件暴露-反应曲线的分离可能反映潜在效应修饰,但也可能源于非线性主效应、气象因素间的相关性及联合暴露空间的非均匀经验支持。江淮丘陵区更强的联合气象效应与该区域较高的SFTS发病率在空间上一致,提示该区域可能具有更有利于SFTS传播的气象-生态背景。 流行病学特征:2011—2023年安徽省共报告5,715例SFTS病例,居全国第三位,其中84.74%为农民。累计病例数超过100例的8个城市(滁州、六安、合肥、安庆、马鞍山、宣城、铜陵、池州)占全省报告病例的95.56%。病例时间分布主要集中在4至7月。 滞后结构选择:城市特异性NB-GAM结果显示,lag01在8个城市中的5个取得最低AIC值,且平均偏差解释度最高(69.9%)。基于模型诊断结果和跨城市一致性,lag01被选定为后续BKMR建模的标准暴露窗口。 变量重要性:PIP结果显示,大气压(平均PIP=0.747)和平均气温(平均PIP=0.735)在所有8个城市中均超过0.5阈值,表现出最高的跨城市平均重要性;降水重要性中等,相对湿度和风速重要性较低。 单独效应:平均气温在多数城市呈倒U型暴露-反应模式,在中位暴露水平的meta分析中显示最大的正向效应(0.034,95% CI 0.010–0.057,P=0.005);大气压亦呈现显著正向效应(0.025,95% CI 0.007–0.042,P=0.006);相对湿度、风速和降水的关联较弱且未达统计学显著。 联合效应与交互作用:8个城市中6个(75%)显示正向联合效应,整体联合效应为0.078(95% CI ?0.032–0.187,P=0.164),呈正向但未达显著。10个两两交互对比的合并估计均包含零,未发现清晰的两两交互证据,城市间异质性低。 区域亚组分析:江淮丘陵区的联合气象效应为0.27(95% CI 0.03–0.50),呈统计学显著正向关联;皖南山区为0.03(95% CI ?0.08–0.15),未达显著。meta回归显示区域间差异未达统计学显著(β=?0.234,95% CI ?0.505–0.037,P=0.087)。 四、讨论与结论 研究发现气象因素对SFTS风险的影响表现为短期滞后效应、非线性暴露-反应关系及显著的地理变异。lag01暴露窗口的生物学合理性在于气象条件可短期内影响长角血蜱的活动、存活和宿主搜寻行为,实验室研究已证实长角血蜱的存活温度阈值为12–40°C,野外观察显示其日活动高峰出现在25–40°C并最活跃于35°C。平均气温和大气压是最重要的气象因素,气温的倒U型关系与蜱传传播的生态特征相符,适宜温度促进蜱的发育和宿主搜寻行为,而过高的温度可能通过增加水分流失抑制蜱的活动。大气压的高显著性可能反映整体天气背景而非对蜱或病原体的直接效应。相对湿度、风速和降水效应较弱但并非生态学上不重要,其效应可能依赖当地气候、地形和植被条件。条件暴露-反应曲线的分离可能反映潜在效应修饰,但也可能源于非线性主效应、气象因素间的相关性及联合暴露空间的非均匀经验支持。江淮丘陵区更强的联合气象效应与该区域较高的SFTS发病率在空间上一致,提示该区域可能具有更有利于SFTS传播的气象-生态背景。 研究结论:安徽省气象因素与SFTS风险之间的关联表现为非线性、联合且地理异质性的暴露-反应模式。短期暴露窗口表现出最佳整体模型性能,平均气温和大气压是最具影响力的气象因素。尽管整体联合效应呈正向趋势,但正式分析未提供稳健两两交互作用的清晰证据,提示观察到的复杂性可能主要反映非线性和情境依赖的响应而非强烈的气象协同作用。区域分析进一步提示江淮丘陵区可能存在更强的联合气象效应。这些发现强调了联合考虑多种气象因素及其非线性关系、短期时间模式和区域生态背景的重要性,为制定因地制宜的SFTS风险评估和早期预警策略提供依据。 news.content: Thailand News Thailand news, politics, business, crime, and lifestyle—get breaking updates from Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Pattaya, and beyond. Stay informed on Thai society, economy, tourism, and expat life with The Thaiger. - Cambodian bridal studio accused of copying Queen Suthida’s gownA Thai Facebook page says a Cambodian wedding studio copied a bespoke gown made for Queen Suthida by Atelier Pichita, and sold it as a collection inspired by the 1890s. - Khao Kheow zoo welcomes white rhino calf on World Rhino DayKhao Kheow Open Zoo has welcomed a new male white rhino calf, announcing the arrival on September 22 as the zoo marked World Rhino Day 2026. The calf was born to Grietjie and Sudi following a pregnancy of more than 16 months. Zoo staff said the newborn is healthy and has already been able to stand and nurse from his... - Former park official defends his decision to drive through elephantsA former assistant to the head of Khao Yai National Park disputed a fine issued after a video showed his sedan passing close to two wild elephants on a road inside the park. The driver, identified as Saroj Praphan, faced criticism after footage showed his sedan driving towards two elephants while tourists were gathered nearby taking photographs. Khao Yai National Park... - Thailand, Russia plan 130th anniversary celebrationsThailand and Russia are preparing cultural celebrations to mark 130 years of diplomatic relations in 2027, with their culture ministers meeting in Russia to discuss artistic exchanges and ways to promote Thailand’s creative economy internationally. Thai Culture Minister Sabida Thaised met her Russian counterpart, Olga Lyubimova, at Russia’s Ministry of Culture yesterday, September 22. The meeting focused on preparations for... - Thailand faces flash floods as downpours hit September 23–27The Thai Meteorological Department (TMD) issued another heavy rain warning for Thailand from today, September 23, through September 27, with very heavy rain expected in some areas and an increased risk of flash floods and run-off. The lower Northeast and East are expected to be affected first, before the rain spreads to the North, Central Thailand, including Bangkok and surrounding... - Minister probes 100m baht Israeli-linked land purchasesDeputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwanchawee says he will personally investigate reports that Israeli-linked companies have bought land worth nearly 100 million baht in Thailand’s three southern border provinces, as officials expand checks on Chabad centres in Thailand. Speaking at the Bhumjaithai Party today, September 22, Polapee said officials were examining around eight or nine Chabad sites nationwide, including existing centres... - Sattahip fishing boat sinking leaves 3 dead, 4 missingThree people have died, and four remain missing after a fishing boat sank off Sattahip in Chon Buri, prompting the Thai navy to deploy a patrol vessel, helicopter and special operations personnel in an ongoing search. The fishing boat involved was the Sor Kanchanawaree 888, which had 22 people aboard. Fifteen were rescued, while seven were initially reported missing. Amarin TV reported at... - Young Thai doctors quit over system pressures, not long hours aloneNearly 1,000 doctors a year are leaving Thailand’s public healthcare system, according to the head of a young doctors’ network, who says heavy workloads, burnout and structural problems are pushing many out despite continued demand. Dr Supanan Janeteerawong, president of the Thai Junior Doctor Network, said today, September 22, that many doctors she had spoken to still wanted to practise... - Cambodian user claims jong kraben after Thai crew’s London appearanceA Cambodian netizen has claimed that jong kraben-style clothing has long existed in Cambodia after seeing Bangkok Airways cabin crew wearing the style in London, prompting Thai responses over the outfit’s historical roots. The claim followed footage of Bangkok Airways crew posted on September 18, appearing at Horse Guards Parade in London in contemporary blue Thai-inspired outfits matching the airline’s... - Family of Thai woman in Germany seek help after five weeks without contactA Thai woman turned to social media to search for her missing older sister, who moved to Bavaria, Germany, after marrying a German man and has been out of contact with her family in Thailand for more than a month. The woman, identified as Karatploy Kub, shared details of her missing 43 year old sister, Lapasrada Stenzel, in the Facebook... - 93 year old woman donates four land plots to Priest HospitalA 93 year old woman donated four vacant plots of land to Priest Hospital yesterday, September 21, to support the treatment and care of sick Buddhist monks and novices. The donor, Manatsiri Ampunan, who holds the rank of special group captain, gave three plots measuring about 800 square metres each, along with a fourth plot measuring about 240 square metres.... - Thailand video news | Bangkok riverside communities put on alert as Chao Phraya levels rise, Chon Buri reviews more than 14,000 foreign-linked companies for nominee risksIn Thailand video news, Alex covers news stories from across Thailand and Asia. The stories include Bangkok city officials are putting communities on alert as Chao Phraya levels are set to rise, then in Chon Buri, more than 14,000 foreign-linked companies have been flagged for nominee risk, in smuggling news, four suspects have been indicted in a heroin network and... - Buakaw brings Muay Thai to Washington DC festivalThe two-time K-1 World MAX champion demonstrated Thai fighting techniques for visitors at the Sawasdee DC Thai Festival on Pennsylvania Avenue. - Queen Sirikit cremation schedule confirmed for DecemberThe Queen Sirikit royal cremation will take place over five days from December 15 to 19, with the main cremation ceremony scheduled for December 16 at Sanam Luang in Bangkok. The programme was conveyed by the Bureau of the Royal Household and acknowledged at a Public Relations Committee meeting yesterday, September 21. The ceremonies will begin at 5pm on December... - Thailand protests Miss Universe Cambodia over historic photoThailand’s Ministry of Culture plans to issue a formal protest to the organisers of Miss Universe Cambodia 2026 after a historical Thai photograph appeared in a video presentation about Cambodian dress culture. In a statement released yesterday, September 21, Culture Minister Sabeeda Thaised said the image shown during the pageant was the photograph known as “Siamese Woman of Kamphaeng Phet”,... - Korat shopper buys gold ring online for 6,730 baht but it’s fakeShe paid in three instalments for a 1.9-gramme ring shipped from overseas. A gold shop told her it was not real gold, and the seller had already closed down. A woman in Nakhon Ratchasima says she was sold a fake gold ring through a popular shopping app. She has shared her story as a warning to other online shoppers. The... - Family of Korat woman killed in Taiwan seek help bringing her ashes homeThe family of a Thai woman found dead in a freezer in Taiwan have asked the Thai government to help bring her ashes and belongings home, and to tell them whether they can seek compensation from the man accused of killing her. The 36-year-old, from Phimai district in Nakhon Ratchasima and known to her family as Jeans, was found in... - Sa Kaeo abbot swept into drain while clearing debrisAn abbot in Sa Kaeo died after being swept through a drainage pipe while clearing vegetation and debris from a waterway following hours of heavy rain in Wang Nam Yen district yesterday, September 20. Rescue volunteers from the Sawang Sa Kaeo Foundation’s Wang Nam Yen unit were called to the meditation centre at about 4.30pm. Residents had already pulled the monk... - Thailand solar panel imports surge ahead of household schemeThailand’s solar panel imports jumped 88.7% year on year to US$426.7 million, around 14.93 billion baht, during the first seven months of 2026, with China accounting for almost the entire market. According to The Nation, citing figures from the Ministry of Commerce and Customs Department, the January to July increase marked a sharp recovery after import values contracted during both... - Trail runner dies after collapse during 25km race in TakA male trail runner died after collapsing about 14 kilometres into a 25-kilometre race in Tak province yesterday, September 20, despite fellow competitors attempting CPR. The incident was first reported on Facebook in the Thai group Trail Running – Chat, where a user said the man lost consciousness at around the 14-kilometre point. Other runners stopped to provide CPR but... - Andros Townsend run over by pitch roller in Thai LeagueFormer England international Andros Townsend was run over by a pitch roller while warming up at half-time during a Thai League 1 match, but escaped serious injury and later came on in stoppage time. The incident happened during Pattani FC’s 3-0 home defeat to PT Prachuap FC at Tinsulanon Stadium yesterday, September 19. Townsend, who was among the substitutes for... - Chon Buri man dies trying to save newborn puppies from floodA man has died inside a burrow in Chon Buri after going in to reach newborn puppies he feared would be flooded. Two of the puppies were found dead beside him. Wanna Sae Li, 65, crawled into a burrow beside a drainage canal in Ban Bueng as the rain rose. Rescuers had to dig him out and found two newborn... - Songkhla woman dies after falling more than 10 metres at Pha Taem fallsThe 48-year-old tourist slipped while photographing the second tier of Kwang Tone waterfall in Pha Taem National Park on September 18. Rescuers walked three kilometres of forest trail and took more than two hours to reach her. A woman has died after falling more than 10 metres at a waterfall in Pha Taem National Park in Ubon Ratchathani. She had... - Princess Sirivannavari leads Chud Thai showcase in TokyoPrincess Sirivannavari Nariratana Rajakanya has presented all eight styles of Chud Thai Phra Ratchaniyom in Tokyo as Thailand continues its push for UNESCO recognition of the national costume tradition. The Princess presided over the presentation on September 18 at the Hyokeikan building of the Tokyo National Museum, where three styles of traditional men’s Suea Phra Ratchathan shirts were also showcased.... - Open beer found after woman goes on crash spree in Chon BuriA woman was detained after crashing into shops and a motorcyclist in Chon Buri before residents chased her for more than three kilometres, with police later finding an open beer bottle inside her car. Nong Prue Police Station was alerted at around 10.10pm yesterday, September 19, to the incident in Soi Wat Boonsamphan, Khao Noi, Bang Lamung district. At the... - Korat couple turns 180 baht into 12 million baht lottery winA 39 year old general worker and his 38 year old wife in Nakhon Ratchasima have won 12 million baht (US$367,000) in the September 16 lottery draw after paying just 180 baht for two tickets, chosen because the ending 640 caught the wife’s eye. The couple are Phitsanu Warin, a general worker, and Panatda Suwannarat, a private-sector employee. They hold... - Speeding driver blamed for scaring wild elephants in Khao YaiWild elephant lovers criticised a driver online yesterday, September 19, after a car reportedly sped past a father and calf crossing a road in Khao Yai National Park. A political party leader is now urging the park chief to take disciplinary action against the man. The two wild elephants, Pho Ngathong and Tonkla, were walking across the road when the... - Thai Navy picks Hanwha Ocean of South Korea for 16.73 billion baht frigateHanwha Ocean of South Korea has been selected to build a new frigate for the Royal Thai Navy, in a 16.73 billion baht (about US$496 million) deal the navy says was awarded through a transparent, rules based process. The result was announced on Friday, September 18, at an 11am press conference in the Chao Phraya Room at the navy auditorium.... - Thailand adds Legionnaires, SFTS, RSV and shingles to disease watch listThailand has added four more illnesses, Legionnaires’ disease, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), RSV and shingles, to its list of notifiable diseases, meaning doctors and hospitals must now report every case to the Department of Disease Control. The national communicable disease committee approved the draft notification on Friday, September 18, during its fifth meeting of the year, held at... - Nonthaburi vehicle inspection centres lose licences over false certificatesThree vehicle inspection centres in Nonthaburi have had their operating licences revoked after regulators found they issued roadworthiness certificates that did not match the vehicles, in some cases without inspecting them at all.
